- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 3+ days of -0.00 or -0.33), model underestimates; add 2-5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags 1-2 days behind true price movement; shift forecast 1-2 days ahead if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (e.g., alternating 0.33 and -0.00), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-7 days to anchor forecast.
